task.description:
Three gaps, one theme: a plan can be lost without anyone being told.

1. plan set REPLACES the whole plan. Passing only --file and --summary silently dropped six recorded steps on SP-29; the call reported success. Observed live, not theorised.
2. Nothing queries the next unfinished step. plan step can mark one complete and plan show prints the list, but a briefing cannot say what to do next without the reader parsing rows.
3. Nothing refuses to destroy progress. A plan with completed steps can be overwritten by a plan that has none, and the completion history goes with it.

PROPOSED, smallest honest shape:
  plan set --file F            merges: keeps recorded step state for step ids that still exist
  plan set --file F --replace   the current behaviour, explicit
  plan set ... (no --force)     refuses when the update would DROP a completed step
  plan next                     prints the first unfinished step and its gate
  plan show / briefing          renders progress as n/m so truncation is visible at a glance

Why not just make it additive: a plan that cannot be corrected is a plan nobody maintains. The rule is not that plans are immutable - it is that destroying recorded progress must be asked for.

NOT overkill, and the reason is the pattern this suite keeps removing: a call that reports success while discarding what it was given. SP-30 records the replace half.
task.title: Plans should carry their progress: query the next step, and refuse to drop a completed one without being asked
